Definition: from a derivative of G5087; something put down, i.e. a substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively):--foundation.
BiblicalUsage: themélios is the Bible's word for a foundation. In Luke 6:48, laid the foundation on a rock. Across its 14 occurrences, the word keeps that same sense, whether the setting is promise or warning.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that no life stands without a foundation, and Christ is the only one that holds. That is why I hold themélios fast when easier words tempt me away.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
